title: Baker Boy Takes Album, Song and Film Clip of the Year at 2026 NIMAs
summary: The Yolŋu rapper first broke through in 2017 after winning triple j's Unearthed National Indigenous Music Awards competition.
body: Baker Boy was the dominant winner at the 2026 National Indigenous Music Awards, taking home three of the night’s top prizes at a ceremony held Saturday (Aug. 8) at the Darwin Amphitheater. The Yolŋu rapper won Album of the Year for DJANDJAY , while his single “THICK SKIN” — featuring Thelma Plum, Emma Donovan, Kee’ahn and Jada Weazel — claimed both Song of the Year and Film Clip of the Year. Baker Boy performed the track live at the ceremony, bringing out Donovan as a surprise guest. Cousin duo Birdz and Fred Leone won Artist of the Year, their first NIMA, on the strength of their debut EP GIRA . Drifting Clouds took Best New Talent, Northern Peninsula Area won Community Clip of the Year for “All The Way From The NPA,” and Bulman School & Community earned the Indigenous Language Award for “LOK LOK MAH BURARR” (Lizard & Goanna). body: Vera Blue has taken on one of alternative rock’s most enduring songs, covering Radiohead ‘s “Creep” for triple j’s Like A Version . The Australian singer-songwriter stripped the 1992 track back to three elements — electric guitar, piano and vocals — building from the lower end of her range into a soaring falsetto by the chorus. Late in the performance she deployed The Pipe, a mouth-controlled dynamic effects processor and synthesizer made by SOMA Laboratory, adding an eerie texture to the arrangement. Blue said she was drawn to the song’s emotional core, describing “Creep” as an “epic rock song” whose lyrics are also “heartbreaking,” and aiming for a “very haunting version” that still nods to Thom Yorke’s original. Blue also performed “Maze,” a track from her forthcoming album Modern Rituals , during her studio session.
